The field of programmable network switches has grown significantly over the last five years, evolving from a niche, closed-source domain into an area characterized by extensive contributions across various research groups. However, integrating these contributions into functional hardware remains difficult, primarily because few open-source compiler back-ends exist to validate programs end-to-ends. Furthermore, diverse programming models demand different backend supports, and existing simulators like Mikey often lack the granularity for rigorous verification while failing to match the performance of real hardware. To address these challenges, we introduce OpenFlowPlus, a versatile software stack designed for programmable switches that runs seamlessly on commercial off-the-shelf hardware alongside specialized platforms like Intel's Data Center Online Transform (DCN T). Built upon an advanced P4 foundation, OpenOfowPlus offers comprehensive control over planar switching fabrics, enables robust data plane validation utilizing Valsim, incorporates streamlined management capabilities through a minimalist framework, and ensures adaptable functionality through an extensible architecture.

This study presents a modified mixed finite element formulation designed to handle the vector transport equation, designed to be paired with any standard finite volume approach used for pressure. By directly resolving the momentum equation and incorporating a pressure-robust selection of pressure gradients and mesh types, this method enhances mass conservation and yields superior resolution of the velocity field relative to traditional strategies. Specifically, it eliminates standard pressure errors and ensures that solutions along advection paths remain largely independent of the pressure field. Furthermore, the robustness of the algorithm is significantly amplified when utilizing perpendicular or anisotropic mesh configurations. The formulation's effectiveness is validated through tests on both analytical and complex, real-world cases—such as those derived from meteorology and medical imaging—demonstrating significant improvements in mass conservation.

Recent years have seen significant development in ethical machine learning, particularly regarding the roles of federated learning (FL) and differential privacy (DP) in tackling fairness concerns. However, we identify a notable tradeoff: ensuring a specific level of fairness via DP inevitably leads to substantial model utility losses, which can be further intensified by multiple client participation in FL. Furthermore, our findings indicate that achieving fairness through fairness constraints alone requires DP-FL solutions built upon unbiased local model aggregations.

Human Video Understanding (HAN) is a proposed hierarchical architecture designed to address the core challenges of video comprehension: spatial-temporal scene analysis, object hierarchy, and temporal progression. In models involving an isolated wave packet scalar field falling into an isolated charged black hole, two distinct outcome regimes emerge based on the charge-to-extremality ratio. In the near-extremal regime, the final stationary state remains a black hole, with all scattered energy ultimately settling in its electromagnetic components. Conversely, in the extremalm regime, the resulting object is an accelerated, moving charge representing the black hole's core, with every unit of scattered energy allocated entirely to the surrounding spacetime. By applying the first law of black hole mechanics to this charged moving body in this extreme case, one derives the black hole entropy area law, confirming the validity of physical principles across these divergent scenarios.

Star formation is a central area of research in astronomy, essential for understanding how chemical elements are synthesized and the evolution of galaxies, with significant implications for tracing the cosmic history of life's origins. Consequently, mastering the star formation process requires analyzing diverse systems across various spatial and temporal scales. It begins with an overview of observational techniques and astrophysical contexts for isolated to bound star formation, followed by a numerical exploration covering the formation, mass growth, and evolution of protostars, as well as the mechanisms driving stellar mass loss. Multimodal optimization generally aims to identify multiple distinct local optima within a specific objective function, whereas multi-objective optimization seeks various trade-off solutions across conflicting objectives. Although these two approaches differ significantly, the visualization methods developed for revealing Pareto fronts have been partially adapted by some researchers to expose distinct optima. However, these related works frequently fail to optimize the resulting visual solutions; they merely organize existing, unoptimized solution points into visual representations, thereby neglecting the actual optimization process. In multi-objective optimization visual guides by contrast, interactive elements transform the visualized result into an optimized one, enabling decision-makers to guide the search process toward preferred outcomes. This research introduces a similar interactive framework for multimodal optimization. Its primary innovation is the capacity to optimize distinct local optima rather than merely displaying the current search results. By transforming the visual representation into an optimized result, users can engage in a co-evolutionary process with the simulation to manually select between different optimized outcomes. To achieve this, we adapt a multi-objective visualization technique designed around the concept of a "local niche," which formulates a specific sub-problem. This sub-problem minimizes the objective function value while simultaneously maximizing the degree of separation (distance) between the user's current visual estimate and any pre-existing local optima. Through interactive manipulation of this visualization tool—adjusting parameters to add, remove, or modify local optima as needed—users can directly incorporate their knowledge into the optimization simulation. A common challenge in imitation learning is a domain shift between the environment where an expert generates demonstrations and the lagging environment employed by the student agent, potentially causing learning failures. Since perfect environment alignment is often elusive, there is a critical need to make training robust to such disparities. This work presents a new behavior-centric reinforcement learning algorithm designed to mitigate these differences without requiring access to specific environment states; it operates instead on available state-value estimates and state-transitions. Additionally, a new metric is developed to quantify the distance between student and teacher states within these abstract representations, offering both a diagnostic tool for detecting environment bias and a method to stabilize learning. Experiments conducted on the standard Atari benchmark confirm that this approach significantly improves sample efficiency and performance consistency across varying environment implementations.

Association rules constitute an interpretable format for revealing significant yet specific localized patterns within data; consequently, data mining strategies frequently aim to generate an association rule set that is both relevant and easy to comprehend. This study examines redundancy among associated rules by analyzing their structural interconnections and defining redundancy as the logical relationship of one rule being strictly implied by another. We characterize redundancy using the model of partial orders defined by logical entailment, proposing that algorithmic detection of such implicit redundancy can significantly refine an associated rule set to enhance interpretability. Since identifying elements hidden in partial orders requires determining their Maximal Elements, we present an algorithm specifically designed to compute this element for our rules. We validate this approach using synthetic datasets, real-world data, and domain-specific rules. Through this analysis, we demonstrate that considering implicit logical redundancy significantly augments our understanding of association rule sets.

Cryptographic commitments are commonly employed in privacy-preserving data management systems (PP-DBs) to hide value comparisons during cryptographic operations. While effective, this approach ignores potential real-world dependencies between records that could exacerbate privacy risks if left unaccounted for. We address this limitation by introducing a new threat model and corresponding attack framework capable of deducing dependencies even when commitments prevent value comparisons. We propose two specific attacks—a binary attack applicable to general dependencies and a transitivity attack for dependency chains—and demonstrate via implementation that these are practically feasible against real-world datasets beyond synthetic test cases. Consequently, we outline refined protocols that enable robust binary privacy attacks within PP-DB environments and suggest modifications to reduce reliance on commitment schemes.

Federated Learning (FL) stands as a privacy-centric machine learning framework that avoids collecting sensitive data by distributing model training across edge devices. Although widely adopted for its privacy advantages, FL struggles with scalability due to bandwidth limitations during frequent global communication rounds. To address this challenges, this paper introduces **BuffFed**, a novel algorithm designed to boost FL scalability and preserve privacy independently of dataset size. BuffFed functions by having clients upload small data subsets containing unlabelled data and partial model updates periodically instead of waiting for full datasets throughout entire rounds, thereby continuously offloading computation to reduce memory usage and enhance scalability independently. Crucially, this approach remains secure as long as the periodic sampling remains unconnected to unlinked partial data, ensuring unattainable inference without full private information leakage. Furthermore, we establish that BuffFed maintains convergence rates comparable with those of conventional FL algorithms under identical conditions, alongside providing rigorous theoretical assurances that global minimum values remain private with probability one, barring accidental sampling leaks. Experimental evaluations reveal significant performance gains: BuffFed exceeds current FL methods in scaling capabilities by a factor of 10x while retaining 10x greater privacy.

Although the traditional Hawking radiation framework suggests that primordial black holes (PBHs) cannot serve as the entirety of dark matter across standard mass ranges, we demonstrate that when information-preserving quantum effects on Hawking evaporation are accounted for, this limitation is removed. Our findings indicate that it is now feasible—considering the modified spectra—for PBHs within the mass window of $10^{8}$ to $10^{9}$ kilograms to account for 100% of dark matter. This quantum correction also imposes stringent constraints on the PBH formation mechanism.

This work examines a dynamic crack phenomenon within a particle-raised fluid system. As the solid-like particle assembly fails and opens up like an elongating crack, two opposing mechanisms govern the system's dynamics: initial rupture drives a hydrodynamic expansion of the fluid, while particle reunion counteracts this separation. The resulting equilibrium between rafts is determined by how quickly particles re-aggregate relative to the stretching force. Maintaining a consistent spacing requires that particle diffusion scales appropriately, specifically that the time for a particle to travel the distance to the nearest edge ($t_d \sim l^2/D$) remains invariant as the rupture spacing ($l$) varies. By comparing this with experimental observations of particle rafts, the findings validate the theoretical model and allow for the determination of how solid-like properties—specifically shear modulus ($G'$) and yield stress ($\tau_y$)—govern the distance between ruptures. The study concludes by suggesting potential applications in understanding disease-related blood clot dynamics and the formation of microcracks in bio-materials like bone or dentin.

We evaluate OLEO-Learn against leading alternatives using two established benchmarks: a cognitive test for primary school students and a dataset covering general knowledge for children. This study introduces a novel spectrogram-based perceptual loss function that captures high-frequency structure in the generated audio by leveraging its spectral characteristics. The training pipeline involves training an external encoder on randomly sampled spectrograms to identify dominant high-frequency patterns, which are subsequently encoded to predict the original spectrograms via a regression task. By integrating this external high-frequency pattern analysis into training, a specialized loss term isolates and minimizes high-frequency discrepancies between target and generated spectrograms, allowing low-frequency structure discrepancies to remain unaltered. Tests on the MIR data spectrograms demonstrate that incorporating this perceptual loss enhances frequency stability, resulting in spectrograms with less fluctuation and smoother patterns. Additionally, applying the proposed method to ESC-50 and Urban Sound 8C datasets improves audio synthesis fidelity compared to models lacking this external loss mechanism.

Fully Connected Recurrent Neural Networks (FCRNNs), representing a fundamental class of Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), have long struggled with effective training, although recent efforts such as connected convolutional FCRNNs (ccFNNs) have largely alleviated this issue. Utilizing our variational autoencoder (VAE) framework, we have constructed VAE-based FCRNNs (VFRNNs) capable of generating well-organized, structured latent manifold representations free from inter-layer dependencies, thereby eliminating the traditional training hurdles associated with fully connected architectures. Additionally, we have introduced a novel training methodology based on self-denoising autoencoders that requires no target labels. In this approach, synthetic noise is randomly applied to specific layers, which are subsequently omitted during forward and backward propagation forces the model to reconstruct the hidden state based solely on the output from the noisy path, effectively reinforcing the recurrence function through this optimization process. Empirical evaluations across multiple data benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed architecture not only achieves competitive or superior performance relative to existing state-of-the-art models but also substantially accelerates the training speed.

This paper introduces DataScope, a visualization framework dedicated to debugging machine learning (ML) pipelines through direct interaction with live data flows. Existing approaches typically rely on static snapshots or compressed summaries, which often obscure root causes of issues in broad datasets or narrow visualization scopes. In contrast, DataScope offers a flexible design that supports concurrent views of diverse data representations and facilitates interactive exploration across temporal moments. Empirical testing involving both domain experts and skilled but intermediate users demonstrates the framework's ability to identify three specific failure modes in extensive pipelines: incorrect data loading, model-training irrelevancies, and, to a lesser extent, domain shifts.

Mn$_3$N$_3$ is widely recognized for exhibiting exceptional chiral magnetic properties, such as anomalous Hall effects and topological magnetism, which stem from its unique ferri-magnetic ground state. This state arises from trimerization driven by the material's strong strong anisotropic exchange interactions. In this study, we introduce a highly accurate density functional theory (DFT) approach that explicitly incorporates both anisotropic exchange and the trimerization effect. By extending a previously developed perturbative method for calculating anisotropic exchange to address trimerization, we employ this technique to compare theoretical results with experimental data. Our findings demonstrate that including both phenomena is essential for accurately modeling the material's properties; specifically, accounting for energy changes related to the anisotropic exchange successfully reproduces the experimentally observed lattice constant.

Recovering a hypergraph from its vertex-to-edges mappings (known as hypergraph linearization) is a fundamental problem in graph analytics. While prior studies have achieved this by modeling the process as a degeneracy task, they struggle with very large hypergraphs containing millions of entries and risk generating false edges. Addressing these limitations, we introduce **Hypergraph Reconstruction using Latent factorization (HRL)**—a novel, highly scalable approach capable of accurately handling hypergraphs with up to 4 million nodes and massive edge sets in under a minute. The HRL model employs probabilistic latent factorization to infer an underlying latent structure, enabling meaningful topological reconstruction. By leveraging this latent space to fill a learned probability distribution, HRL estimates the likelihood of potential hyperedges, thereby significantly reducing spurious artifact generation while maintaining speed and accuracy.

Detecting defects in fabric presents significant challenges primarily due to discrepancies in lighting conditions between defects and the background, alongside variations within different textures. To address this, we introduce the Fabric Low-rank Decomposition (FLD) method. This approach processes raw images by decomposing them into a background component and a residual layer containing concentrated defect information. Utilizing deep learning, we subsequently classify these defects. Flaws in the original imagery often exhibit complex patterns that simple lighting contrasts fail to distinguish; however, FEF effectively isolates these anomalies by separating them from the underlying surface. Evaluation on the standard textile dataset indicates a precision of 96.8%, demonstrating competitive performance relative to existing methodologies.

We introduce a novel reinforcement learning approach designed to train agents for navigation in environments characterized by partial observability and stochastic dynamics. By maximizing the mutual information between an agent's movement and its sensory input, the framework aligns with the core principles of information alignment navigation and active inference. Notably, we demonstrate that this method achieves this information alignment through the application of standard value function maximization. Additionally, the framework provides a unified derivation for several foundational strategies in navigation, including goal-directed navigation, information alignment navigation, and active inference. Empirical evaluations confirm that these resulting agents not only reach their targets more frequently but also gather more visual data about their surroundings compared to previous approaches.

We examine the asymptotic behavior of gravitational waves in Brans-Dicke theory when metric and scalar field data are provided on a timelike boundary. For cases where this data fails to be asymptotically smooth, an asymptotic expansion resembling that of asymptotically flat gravity in flat spacetime is constructed. This study addresses the radiation zone ($r\to\infty$) with two scenarios: first, if the metric approaches zero and the scalar field approaches its asymptotic value faster than $r^{-2}$, radiation can reach null infinity unimpeded by the scalar field; second, when radiation information at null infinity is non-zero, specific evolution equations for the radiative components of the scalar field are derived. These equations hold provided certain regularity conditions on the $r\to\infty$ limits of the metric components governing scalar radiation are met.

This study examines the cosmological distribution and peak density of Pop III binary black hole and neutron star remnant mergers through Merger Rate Density (MRD) profiles. These profiles are modeled using self-similar functions of redshift, characterized by a power-law slope and a Gaussian core. We determine these self-similar parameters across four scenarios defined by initial mass function (IMF) sampling strategies and stellar pair separation distributions. Our results indicate that the MRD density peaks at a redshift of $z_{\rm max} \approx 6$, corresponding to the cosmological epoch when the stellar mass density of Pop III stars reached its maximum. At this peak, the MRD density is approximately $1.4 \times 10^{-4} \rm{Gpc^{-3}yr^{-1}}\). Furthermore, we observe that the ratio of binary separation to stellar Jeans length remains largely constant throughout cosmic history. Finally, our analysis reveals that the overall gravitational wave event rate from Pop III binaries is highly sensitive to uncertainties in stellar mass sampling from the IMF; specifically, rate estimates for binary neutron stars and binary black holes vary by a factor of 10 and three orders of magnitude, respectively.

Simulations utilizing synthetic data confirm that these techniques remain robust even in noisy environments, successfully accommodating inherent inaccuracies typical of estimated load and topology data.

This study introduces a multi-phase training framework designed to establish robust canonical poses for 3D objects within the canonicalization problem. To facilitate effective learning at each phase, our method incorporates a features-based canonicalization strategy alongside a shape-based one, combining them to define multiple shape and canonical loss functions. Crucially, we utilize a shape-decanonicalization network as an intermediate tool to generate shape estimates. These estimates then function as a shape reference, enabling a self-supervised mechanism that ensures the final canonical pose adheres to consistent shape properties. Empirical results demonstrate that this approach significantly outperforms existing methods on standard datasets without requiring shape references during inference. Additionally, we provide visual evidence confirming the formation of stable shape-centric features throughout both training and testing phases.

Although the pandemic significantly accelerated the distribution of vaccines globally, various clusters of uninfected individuals have delayed acceptance due in part to circulating vaccine doubts fueled by online falsehoods. To address this hurdle uniquely, a proposed novel integrative framework combines social network analysis (SNA) and automated content analysis (ACA) to monitor and analyze social media interactions related to vaccine misinformation and skepticism. Applying SNA and ACA to extensive Twitter datasets related to COVID-19, the study identifies distinct communities and scrutinizes internal discourse through automated methods. Findings indicate that ACA is effective in perceiving nuanced expressions doubt and hesitation, while SNA provides robust network-level insights into how misinformation persists within isolated groups, explaining the ineffectiveness of external corrective efforts. Ultimately, this framework offers a transferable methodology for investigating online attitudes toward vaccine doubts and falsehoods more broadly and can be utilized to design targeted strategies to boost acceptance rates.

We conducted a statistical study on a sample of 100 potential exo-Earths identified within the habitable zones of G-type stars using NASA's EXOEarths database. Utilizing the ExoStrate model, we modeled their mineralogies and interior structures based on observed mass and radius data for each planet. Our analysis employed a Monte Carlo approach, creating 1,000 realizations by randomly sampling within measurement uncertainty intervals for mass and radius under a uniform prior distribution for internal fractional compositions. Results indicate that these potential exo-Earths exhibit similar external mass-radius characteristics to Earth but often possess divergent internal structures and surface compositions despite matching host star conditions. Although unimodal distributions for mass-radius and fractional composition variables suggest that some values align closely with Earth's values (e.g., mantle, core fractions), achieving such specific values appears statistically random rather than deterministic. Consequently, these systems likely never reached a system-wide steady equilibrium matching Earth's precise internal architecture due to historical divergences. We posit that variations arise because different planets underwent distinct accretional and dynamical thermal processes; thus, statistical averages alone cannot be used to infer the actual states of specific exoplanets without applying similarly restrictive predictive models.

On a standard dataset, our proposed attention mechanism delivers a mean throughput gain of 111% over traditional methods.

Double Parton Distribution Functions (DPDFs) provide insight into the spatial correlation of partons within the same proton, going beyond the information given by standard Parton Distribution Functions (PDFs). Because kinematic constraints between two particles are not always present in all processes, a framework utilizing such constraints can significantly differentiate DPDs from PDFs in terms of extractability. Martian and lunar reguli serve as abundant extraterrestrial sources suitable for various construction applications and 3D manufacturing. This study investigates the interaction between laser and lunar reguli LORR within the context of selective laser sintering (SLS), a process utilized to build functional structures using fine, loose powders. A fundamental relationship between deposited energy density and particle motion governs SLS; therefore, this paper employs a thermo-structural model to examine the thermal history of the laser-reguli interaction and explore emerging research into sintering lunar dust. Results indicate that both rotational velocity and translational movement of lunar reguli particles significantly influence the sintering outcome on SLS. Furthermore, effective quality assurance requires a consistent relative motion pattern among the laser beam, powder feed, and build table throughout the entire SLS operation.

Using $JWST$'s Beta (Br) luminosity as an estimate for star formation efficiency (SFR) provides an independent benchmark to validate the SFR precision produced by Prospector's Bayesian inference methods. Prospector integrates complex stellar evolution models and spectral synthesis codes, along with cosmological parameters and chemical abundances as parameters, facilitating the analysis of observed spectra through comprehensive likelihood inference. By applying this framework alongside the Beta SFR formula using simulated Prospector priors based on near-infrared data from the simulated NIRCam instrument and simulating realistic observational impacts like noise and surface brightness constraints, we established the reliability of both estimation techniques across SFR and stellar mass ranges relevant to upcoming $JWST$ observations. Although considerable scatter remains due to stochastic star formation, we demonstrate that Prospector can recover $JWST$ Beta luminosity to an accuracy of roughly 30% when utilizing appropriately constructed priors. Finally, we discuss the correlation between the prior scope and resulting inference spread, emphasizing the critical role $JWST$ plays in empirically refining star formation rate determinations for high-redshift galaxies through precise measurements.

We demonstrate a connection between exceptional braided auto-equivalences of orbifolds and quadratic categories, revealing that these equivalences are always "fractional" (non-invertible) in light of recent research. Specifically, we establish a bijection between the set of these equivalences and the set of quadratic categories. Since these equivalences are non-invertible, implying there are both left and right versions, we examine their impact on global symmetries and conclude that such transformations necessarily result in fractional global symmetries. Furthermore, we analyze the roles these equivalences play in (co)dimensional zero anomalies and prove that these anomalies are fractional as well. The findings also clarify the relationship between these equivalences and T-duality, showing that, similar to T-duality, they are fractional.

This paper addresses Participant 2 of the UbiComp 2021 Challenge, aiming to decode handwritten notes from a user holding a sensor-equipped device. The approach first pinpoints the activity related to writing by analyzing the device's time-series sensor data using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. Once writing is detected, the corresponding characters are identified through a Memory Matrix Transformer (MMT) model applied to the data patterns; this involves matching a note's sensor fingerprint against pre-established sensor templates for individual characters. Finally, a template-driven template selection method is introduced to decouple these examples from a library of character templates, enabling the extraction of sensor data corresponding to specific letters or symbols.

This study introduces a novel approach to modeling duration through a discrete mixture distribution by employing discrete Gaussian mixtures. Leveraging Bayesian inference, the paper implements a series of updating algorithms for model parameters based on completed, in-progress, and terminated observations. A new scheme for determining the most probable duration emerges from the posterior distribution when durations remain incomplete. Applications of this method across two datasets are presented to assess its performance. Furthermore, discussions highlight implications regarding self-selection biases arising from censored incomplete data.

Accurately identifying locations in spatial ecology and related domains remains a difficult task. This study presents a Bayesian approach to occupancy modeling that integrates location uncertainty by conditioning on probability distributions instead of precise point coordinates. Rather than restricting ourselves to standard normal distributions, we employ flexible Bayesian nonparametric methods to derive prior distributions for our location uncertainty. Simulations demonstrate that our approach and its associated estimators perform well. We also apply this model to two ecological scenarios: estimating bird populations based on potentially imprecise telemetry readings and analyzing whale sightings derived from aerial sonar data.

This paper presents an analysis of the Skincare project, which introduces a diagnostic system for identifying and recommending treatments for various skin conditions. Designed to empower general practitioners and dermatologists with advanced dermatological expertise, the system relies on image analysis to automatically classify anomalies. The system posits that characteristic images containing defects can be labeled by comparing them against normal images of healthy skin; subsequently, any subsequent image is automatically assessed for defects through image-to-image comparison methodologies. Extracting inter-beat intervals (IBIs) from noisy electrocardiogram (ECG) signals is a critical initial step for quantifying heart rate variability (HRV). Traditional methods rely on conventional signal processing techniques that often fall short when faced with low-quality data, whereas deep-learning approaches have emerged as powerful alternatives capable of learning intrinsic features automatically. This study introduces a novel deep-learning framework using fully convolutional networks (FCN) to precisely derive IBI sequences from noisy ECG inputs. Our model employs multi-scale dilated convolution layers followed by max pooling to effectively handle ECG morphologies at varying durations. By directly regulating time intervals as output, the method avoids post-hoc processing errors. An FCN architecture comprising three upsampling stages achieved the highest testing accuracy of 98.73%. Furthermore, the model demonstrates robustness across entirely new datasets; it reached an accuracy of 98.73% on the St. Petersburg data (SPDBI) collection and 98.40% on the PAMDBI dataset, confirming its reliable performance under diverse conditions.

This study investigates the statistical fluctuations of continuous active forces confined by either harmonic or anharmonic potentials. We introduce a novel technique for achieving photorealistic 3D modeling of human facial expressions by leveraging dynamic texture synthesis. This approach utilizes hierarchical rigid block motion (HUMBI), which estimates spatially consistent landmarks across a hierarchical structure to create corresponding image patches aligned via landmarks and matched using 1-to-1 correspondence. We enhance photorealism by superimposing texture from a single face onto region-level correspondences derived from landmark trees, holding regions steady while warping facial areas to match subject heads. Our contributions include a new algorithm for robust feature tracking using a hierarchical unified framework, a collection of synthetic datasets linking facial expressions to specific facial regions, and a demonstration establishing HUMBI as an effective solution for expressive head modeling through detailed textural synthesis. Our code is available at https://github.com/yzhangcsu/HUMBI.

Within each cascade stage, input data undergoes joint training to produce both intermediate results for specific tasks and final outputs for all tasks simultaneously. Empirical results demonstrate that this cascaded design significantly improves the architecture's learning capability, yielding substantial improvements in performance across all evaluated tasks.

We propose a method that specifically encodes image style into style codes. Our primary objective is to minimize the style image reconstruction error as measured by a perceptual loss function. To achieve this, we develop an encoder that captures stylistic features while avoiding the inclusion of all source imagery. Our approach employs self-attention mechanisms to isolate style without relying on large datasets. Additionally, a decoder utilizing cross-attention to the source image ensures that the encoded style remains distinct from the source content. For images with similar aesthetics, the resulting style codes remain consistent, as our encoder focuses on stylistic nuances rather than full image reconstruction like PCA or VAE. Extensive testing on ImageNet demonstrates this efficacy by showing that applying a generated style from a style image to a content image enhances style transfer quality.

Although visual object classification in video analysis is well-established, extracting meaningful context remains difficult due to noisy and irrelevant data. We propose implementing a dual-stream architecture in which the primary stream acquires the ground context of video content, while the secondary focuses on identifying salient objects. Employing an attentive module within ground context mapping, we filter out unnecessary information to minimize distractions and enhance interpretations of the primary stream. Subsequent temporal awareness is utilized to refine this mapping through frame-by-frame consistency checks and optimization via a contextual module loss mechanism. We evaluated the system across various benchmarks, including MSCOCO, Apache Sennet, and Visual Genome, where results demonstrate consistent improvements over existing methods.

This paper introduces a computational fluid dynamics (CFD) model for two-phase flows, specifically settling snow particles in turbulence, grounded in the probabilistic approach and particle swarm mechanics. Results demonstrate that the proposed settling velocity law effectively captures the influence of particle-swarm hydrodynamics on settlement, while predictions for particle clustering and clustering/dispersion align well with existing experimental data.

The cross-sections for producing deuterons and alpha particles have been theoretically assessed using the ab initio pseudo-adiabatic time-dependent close-coupling (ADCC) framework for the $p+\alpha$ reaction. This study examines two light nuclear targets, $^6$Li and $^8$Be, interacting with linearly polarized ultra-intense laser fields operating at a wavelength of $\lambda = 1\,\mu\text{m}$. Results indicate that the linearly polarized AdCC model strongly supports alpha-particle generation in interactions involving these light, low-Z targets under intense laser irradiation. Notably, the produced $\alpha$ cross-sections exceed those of deuterons by several orders of magnitude. Furthermore, theoretical predictions for minimum kinetic energy align well with experimental observations, while computed angular distributions match measurement data for both produced $p+\alpha$ ions. These findings suggest that linearly polarized intense lasers serve as a viable instrument for investigating ionization, with alpha-emission providing a new avenue to explore ADCC and access nuclear structure information within this interaction regime.

This report introduces the Trident (T4R), a lamprey-inspired bio-inspired robot designed to climb smooth vertical surfaces using locomotion mechanisms analogous to its natural counterpart, the Atlantic Sea Lamprey. Unlike prior robots limited to minimal climb rates relative to this species, the T4R demonstrates the ability to climb at rates three times superior to those of Pacific Lampreys. As depicted by our motion capture system, Trident executes a gait involving localized anchoring movements emulating the biomechanics of real lampreys. Furthermore, system-level analyses indicate that although trunk force contributions are negligible compared to head force, trailing the leading lamprey-style anchoring strategy significantly optimizes climbing performance.
